title: AB 998 (2021-2022 Wisconsin Legislature, regular session): verifying citizenship of individuals on the official voter registration list and contents of operator's licenses and identification cards.
operative_text:
(a_in_person_id) not stated.
(b_no_id_remedy) not stated.
(c_mail_ballot_id) not stated.
(d_proof_of_citizenship) not stated.
(e_other_rule)
(section) s. 5.056 / 5.057 (new): Elections Commission citizenship verification
(quote) The commission shall verify that individuals on the official registration list maintained by the commission under s. 6.36 (1) are U.S. citizens by using the systematic alien verification for entitlements database maintained by the federal Department of Homeland Security.
(section) s. 343.17 (3) (a) 16. (new): legend on license or ID card
(quote) If the person is not a U.S. citizen, the legend “Not valid for voting purposes” or another readily recognizable indication that the license may not be accepted for voter identification purposes.
(other) LRB analysis (printed with the bill): The bill also requires the commission to verify that individuals on the official registration list are U.S. citizens by using the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements database maintained by the federal Department of Homeland Security.
(other) LRB analysis (printed with the bill): Under the bill, the commission must conduct the verifications 60 days before the distribution of absentee ballots to voters before an election.
(other) LRB analysis (printed with the bill): The bill also requires DOT to place on the face of an operator's license or identification card issued to a person who is not a U.S. citizen, the words “Not valid for voting purposes” or another readily recognizable indication that the license may not be accepted for voter identification purposes.
(note) Off this topic: the bill sets no ID or citizenship-proof rule.
